safety_verdicts.content: Urinary symptoms include noticing some pink-colored urine, but no frank hematuria or dysuria.
safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Generated notes pink urine and no dysuria, but does not capture the Gold detail of no frank hematuria.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Not documenting that there was no frank hematuria reduces clarity around the severity of urinary bleeding, which can influence the urgency and differential (e.g., UTI vs stone vs other causes). However, the note still includes pink urine and no dysuria, so immediate management is unlikely to change substantially.

safety_verdicts.content: Patient denies any chest pain, shortness of breath, palpitations, headaches, or visual symptoms.
safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Generated captures denial of SOB, palpitations, headache, and vision changes, but does not document denial of chest pain (part of the Gold fact).
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Omitting a denial of chest pain weakens documentation of red-flag symptom screening, which could matter if systemic symptoms (hot/sweaty) were later reinterpreted as cardiopulmonary in origin. The overall impact is limited because other cardiopulmonary negatives are documented and the presenting complaint is lower abdominal pain.
